title: Private Console: Multi-Cluster Availability Ladder & Safe Rollback Flow
creator: Marco Li
description: Design a compact, scannable availability ladder for private clusters that surfaces cross-cluster dependency risk, region failover readiness, and an actionable safe-rollback flow for operators. The ladder is intended for tenant-facing ops and platform SREs to make quick go/no-go decisions during upgrades and degradations without drilling into logs.
success_metrics: Reduce time-to-decision for upgrade rollbacks from avg 18m to <7m
Reduce follow-up incident tickets related to unclear rollback steps by 40%
Increase operator confidence (survey) to >=80% after 2 weeks of pilot
user_stories: As a platform operator, I want a single lane view showing cluster health tier, degraded signals and safe rollback button, so I can respond quickly during upgrade regressions.
As a tenant owner, I want to see which clusters are currently on canary, stable, or emergency lanes and why, so I can understand potential impact to my traffic.
As an SRE, I want the rollback flow to list pre-checks (capacity, network paths, config drift) and a dry-run result, so I can avoid cascading failures during rollback.
constraints: Must work at 3 different scales: single-tenant cluster, multi-tenant private region (20+ clusters), and enterprise multi-region view
Data freshness: health signals update <=30s; upstream dependency checks (peering/KMS) may be eventual (up to 90s)
No PII or tenant secrets surfaced in UI; only topology and status metadata
Rollbacks must call existing orchestration API; design must not imply direct DB writes from UI
decisions: Use a vertical "ladder" layout instead of horizontal timeline to emphasize escalation paths and rollback triggers
Represent readiness with three tiers: Green (stable), Amber (degraded/warn), Red (fail) with one-click contextual rollback when amber->red threshold exceeded
Include an inline pre-check runner in the rollback modal with compact pass/fail pills and links to diagnostics
Expose a compact 'why' flyout per cluster showing top 3 contributing signals (latency, KV cache miss, egress error rate)
Rollout changes gated behind canary ratio and autoscaling headroom checks to avoid capacity shock during rollback

2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: User interview (3 platform SREs) — they preferred a vertical escalation list; asked for pre-check dry-run and explicit confirmation of traffic drain steps.
2026-03-08 - Eng feedback (Swarna Rao): Implementation concern — running pre-checks synchronously could add latency; proposing async pre-checks with cached last-run results and a 'force-run' option.
2026-03-09 - PM review (Diego Martinez): Prioritize safe-rollback copy and audit trail for compliance. Add link to incident timeline and ability to annotate rollback reason.
2026-03-10 - Design review (Aisha): Updated mocks to include annotations, compact pills and 'rollback dry-run' state. Pushed new prototype and requested accessibility review for colour contrast.
2026-03-11 - Security (Rina Shah): Noted that rollback audit events must not leak tenant identifiers in logs sent to central analytics. Filing follow-up with ENG-9032.

2026-03-12 - QA (Jordan Kim): Proposed acceptance criteria: rollback modal pre-check pass rate must be displayed and rollback button disabled when critical checks fail. Assigned exploratory test cases.
